build_policy: A task-blind builder retains reusable memories with source locators, assigns each entry a task-type and decision-facet applicability tag, and distills anonymous judge failures only into cross-case completeness checks. Exclude case identifiers, product literals, and solution-specific decisions.
consumption_policy: Retrieve only memories whose applicability tags match the current task and active decision facet. Present a compact ranked subset, require repository grounding, and treat task evidence and explicit owner decisions as authoritative when memory conflicts. For specifications, run a generic completeness pass covering omitted versus explicitly invalid configuration, full execution-path scope, runtime failure and retry behavior, lifecycle binding, and consumer-observable acceptance outcomes.
delta: Replace broad direct loading with applicability-routed retrieval to reduce irrelevant-memory burden.
Add task-type and decision-facet tags during memory construction.
Convert anonymous quality gaps into generic specification-completeness checks without preserving case-specific answers.
Rank tightly scoped, repository-grounded, consumer-observable guidance ahead of unrelated workflow or UI guidance.
Make conflict handling explicit: current task evidence and owner decisions override reusable memory.
hypothesis: Applicability-routed memory plus a generic completeness pass will preserve the useful scope, grounding, and behavioral-spec guidance while reducing irrelevant loading and preventing recurring omissions at configuration, failure, retry, and lifecycle boundaries.
